verdict: partly consistent: the enciphered opening and all following groups can be read; one isolated mark at the end of the heading is unassigned.
notes: Read each row from left to right. The first two signs on 105v l.6 read كم, followed by قد حللت من الالغاز معجمة. Both groups كم and قد recur later; the two lām signs in حللت recur in اللغز. This reconstructs the words lost under the repair to 106r l.7, while leaving the physical loss visible. The pointed enclosed mark on 105v l.5 is in the left margin at the end of the Arabic heading; its shape differs from the normal divided-oval fāʾ, and it has no secure repeated value. It could be a heading mark or a prefixed cipher sign (e.g. a variant fāʾ before كم). The alignment places it before the first group without supplying a letter. In 105v l.8 the dotted tooth sign closes اضحت before a divider and لهم; in l.12 the reading نظموا is constrained by recurring ن م و ا, with singleton ẓāʾ assigned by context. The last verse gives قولا لست ادركه / طرطاش طرطش من درديه العكروا. The final wāw–alif are written in full. The cipher uses one sign for لَا in both الالغاز and قولا.
fit_against_record_wording: All 35 groups from 105v l.6 to 106r l.2 can be aligned in the stated direction. The compiler’s clear copy is physically damaged at the opening; recurring signs reconstruct كم قد حللت there. The 105v l.5 mark has indeterminate status independently of the lacuna. Other differences include اضحت لهم, عيص, بها, نظموا, قولا لست, من درديه; context contributes to the singleton readings.

unresolved_positions.evidence: Isolated pointed enclosure with internal loop. Neither the divided oval of the two secure fāʾs nor another occurrence supplies an exact match. The wording from كم onward has an independent sign-by-sign alignment.

opening_reconstruction.clear_copy: The paper repair on 106r l.7 physically removes the opening letters after the initial kāf.
opening_reconstruction.justification: The same kāf-mīm pair occurs in وكم and the same qāf-dāl in قد on 105v l.8. The two lām signs in حللت have numerous examples. The initial ḥāʾ shape matches the one in اضحت. Only a putative prefix before كم is open.
